items.title: Claude Code mods can now read your selection — $.ui.selection() ships in 2.1.288
items.summary: Mods get a new $.ui.selection() call that returns selected text and transcript rows while you're in fullscreen mode — a concrete new surface on top of the Claude Mods launch a day earlier. The same release adds a --max-findings flag to /code-review so you can cap how many findings come back.
items.why: This is the difference between a mod that just watches tool calls and one that actually knows what you've got highlighted on screen right now.
items.action: If you enabled a mod off the Claude Mods launch, check whether it can call $.ui.selection(); otherwise run /code-review --max-findings 5 on your next PR to cut the noise.

eval.reason: A concrete new API surface on the mods system (UI selection access) plus a usability flag, not a routine patch bump.

items.title: Google ships Gemini Interactions API — server-side state so you stop resending the whole conversation
items.summary: The server now tracks conversation history and uploaded files for up to 7 days (or zero-retention if you opt out), runs multi-step tool loops past the old 60-second gateway timeout, and hands you a chronological trace of every turn's reasoning and tool calls.
items.why: Cuts the boilerplate of managing conversation state and tool-call loops yourself, and should lower both cost and latency on anything multi-turn.
items.action: If you've got a Gemini-backed agent hand-rolling its own conversation state, swap one endpoint over to this API and compare latency and cost.

eval.reason: A genuine new API with concrete mechanics (server-managed state, long-running tool loops), not a rehash.

items.title: Sam Altman defends Sign in with ChatGPT as OpenAI opens it to 11 launch partners
items.summary: Plus and Pro subscribers can now log into any of 11 commercial launch-partner apps with ChatGPT and bring their plan usage with them — Business and Enterprise support is coming. Altman's post is a direct response to pushback on why OpenAI built this at all.
items.why: This is OpenAI building an identity-and-entitlement layer other apps can plug into — a real distribution channel, not a feature announcement.
items.action: Worth understanding the OAuth-style flow now if you're building anything that could let a user bring their existing ChatGPT subscription instead of your own billing.

items.title: LangChain cut Open SWE's model bill 64% with a three-tier router — and published how
items.summary: The router runs a classifier on a thread's first message against per-tier criteria built from real LangSmith trace data, sending each request to one of three models along the cost-intelligence frontier. Outcome tracked via merged PRs and user feedback — quality held steady.
items.why: A validated, concrete pattern for not paying frontier prices on every single call in a production coding agent, not just a cost-saving claim.
items.action: Apply the same pattern — base prompt, per-tier criteria, one classifier model — to route calls in one of your own agents and track the before/after cost.

eval.reason: A concrete architecture plus a validated outcome metric (64% cost cut, stable quality), not a listicle.

items.title: How VS Code Went from Monthly to Weekly Releases with AI — Harald Kirschner
items.summary: VS Code's principal PM on moving a 10-year-old, 50M-user product to weekly ships: agent-ready codebases, mandatory AI code review, auto-filed issues from 51 billion daily telemetry events, and VSC-Bench evals. Code written by agents that actually survives to merge rose from 55% to 86%.
